rendered: The micropores of the carbon are about ∼0.5 nm[1] in size. That is too small to accommodate the electrolyte solvent molecule, which is ∼0.7 nm in diameter[2]. The sodium ion is far smaller, only ∼0.2 nm in diameter[3]. Because the solvent cannot enter the pores, the sodium ion must desolvate at the surface of the microporous host and transport independently to the sulfur, so the discharge proceeds as a quasi solid-state reaction at the cathode rather than a conversion reaction with ions moving through the electrolyte to an active site.
